messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — Acme reported a sharp p95/p99 regression in the function-calling flow after the runtime v2.3.1 roll. Baseline p95 was ~260ms, after release p95 sits ~570ms and p99 ~1.1s for routes that enable structured_output + tool router. They attached a trace and a reproducible curl.

alex_runtime: on it. share trace id + sample request and I’ll pull logs and traces.

maria_support: trace link: https://datadog.internal/trace/def456. Repro attached:

maria_support: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"open-proxy-1",
    "input":"Extract order details and call tools if needed",
    "function_call":true,
    "structured_output":{
      "schema":{
        "type":"object",
        "properties":{
          "order_id":{"type":"string"},
          "items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}}
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

ryan_tracing: looked at the flamegraph. Major tail inside validation. Span breakdown (median/95/99 sample): request.receive 6ms, model.generate unchanged ~210ms, tool-router.acquire 8ms, json-schema.validate.sync 140-300ms (big delta), tool-router.dispatch 25ms.

ryan_tracing: synchronous AJV validation appears to be blocking worker threads; load reproduces locally with same curl. Attaching flame.

alex_runtime: we added synchronous AJV validation in v2.3.1 to prevent invalid tool invocations. That sync call was intended to be cheap but looks like it blows up for complex schemas and under high concurrency.

jess_oncall: timeline: v2.3.1 rolled Tue 03:12 UTC. Alerts started Wed afternoon for increased p99s. We need a quick mitigation while runtime crew ships a fix.

alex_runtime: we have a feature toggle enable_structured_validation per-org. Ops can flip for org_0123 to disable sync validation immediately. Consequence: some malformed tool outputs might get forwarded, but we can reduce latency.

maria_support: Acme wants throughput back asap. Approve flip for org_0123.

ci-bot: config-update: override enable_structured_validation=false for org_0123. Propagating (control-plane ~20s, edges ~90s).

alex_runtime: made the change, triggered config refresh for the org. Please validate with customer.

acme_cust: Confirmed — after the flag flip p99 dropped to ~340ms and they see no functional regressions.

alex_runtime: root cause analysis notes:
- AJV sync validate on hot path blocks request workers for complex/dynamic schemas.
- Some code paths compile validators per-request for dynamic schemas; compilation costs ~40-100ms on cold path.
- The dispatcher and validator both parse tool payloads independently causing duplicate CPU work.

alex_runtime: Short-term patch plan:
1) compiled-validator cache for dynamic schemas (cache compiled against schema fingerprint). Expected cold-call reduction ~50-80ms.
2) offload validation to an async worker pool (non-blocking); run a permissive fast-check in request path and enqueue deep validate. For P99 this reduces blocking significantly.
3) introduce schema-node limit and a heuristic "light validate" fallback to avoid pathological schemas.
4) reuse parsed JSON/AST between validator and dispatcher to avoid double-parse.

ryan_tracing: quick perf tests: compiled cache reduces median validation by ~40ms and p99 by ~70ms. Async worker pool (size 8) reduces p99 by ~200ms in our synthetic load.

jess_oncall: near-term actions:
- Keep org override in place for affected customers until patch verified (maria_support)
- Runtime: create P0 ticket for compiled cache + async validator (alex_runtime)
- SRE: temporarily scale up router CPU pool 2x for next 48hrs (sre)
- QA/Security: run full tool-calling regression suite before canary (qa)

alex_runtime: filing ticket INF-4321 with repro, traces, perf numbers and proposed patch. MVP (compiled cache + 1-thread async validator) ETA ~48hrs. Full async streaming + safety heuristics ~2 weeks.

maria_support: updated the SEV with mitigation steps and customer comms. Will keep customer updated and confirm when canary lands.

ryan_tracing: additional note — we should add a metric validation.duration_ms (histogram) and alert on 99th percentile so we detect regressions early. Also instrument schema size (node count) to catch pathological cases.

alex_runtime: agreed. Adding telemetry and a follow-up RFC for AST reuse and long-term async streaming.

maria_support: thanks everyone. Will loop back to Acme after the patch canary. Owners: alex_runtime (fix), ryan_tracing (dashboards/metrics), jess_oncall (mitigation), maria_support (customer comms).
